name: My Life With The Wave Vol 2
editorial_article:
The 'My Life With The Wave' series represents one of the most compelling conceptual projects in modern Detroit deep house, spearheaded by the late, revered producer Mike Huckaby. Rather than relying on his standard studio setup, Huckaby imposed a strict limitation upon himself: crafting an entire record using nothing but sounds derived from the Waldorf Wave synthesizer. This constraint, far from limiting the final output, pushed Huckaby to extract an incredible range of textures—from dusty, organic-feeling percussion and deep, soulful basslines to delicate, fluttering melodies.

Vol 2, released in 2016 on Synth US, stands as a quintessential example of his approach, featuring tracks like 'Let The Dancer Do His Thing' and 'Baseline 313'. The project is notable not just for the music itself, but for its inclusion of an accompanying CD containing 192 samples from the synth, inviting listeners and fellow producers into Huckaby's creative methodology. The resulting sound is quintessential Huckaby—warm, rhythmic, and masterfully layered, bridging the gap between classic Motor City sensibilities and experimental sound design. His ability to evoke deep emotion and floor-moving grooves through such a singular sonic palette cemented his legacy as a true craftsman of electronic music. The project remains a testament to his belief in the power of focus, demonstrating how creative boundaries can serve as a catalyst for innovation rather than a hindrance. His work on this series remains highly sought after by collectors and fans of deep, soulful electronic music worldwide.

editorial_pitch: A masterful exercise in focused constraints, the My Life With The Wave series showcases Mike Huckaby's deep-house ingenuity, utilizing the Waldorf Wave synthesizer as the sole sound source for these warm, rhythmic explorations.
